# everyDock v0.4.1 — English and Korean, clearer icons

A public beta with selectable language, revised defaults for new installations, and permission requests that no longer open two system interfaces at once.

## What's new since v0.4.0

- **English and Korean.** Settings → General → Language offers Follow System, English, and 한국어. Follow System uses Korean for a Korean primary system language and English otherwise. Changes apply without restarting; external app names, filenames, window titles, and native app commands keep their original text.
- **New-install defaults:** Show over Full-Screen Apps is off, and Preview Delay is 0.60 seconds. Existing saved choices are preserved.
- **Separate permission requests and Settings links.** Accessibility and Screen Recording request buttons no longer also open System Settings. Use the macOS dialog's Open System Settings button or everyDock's separately labeled settings links. macOS may suppress repeated permission dialogs.
- **Improved icon rendering.** Display-scale-aware cached artwork and trilinear downsampling preserve available detail. Magnification reuses the cached texture.
- **Updated README.** Includes a multi-monitor image, an English/Korean badge, and a shorter first-install sequence.

Automated checks cover localization/default migration, interpolation, icon rendering, and existing permission/capture behavior. Live bilingual layout, mixed-display icon quality, and fresh-permission dialog sequences still need manual verification. See the [v0.4.1 QA record](https://github.com/hungryZoo/everyDock/blob/main/docs/QA-v0.4.1.md). This remains an ad-hoc signed, unnotarized beta; it is not the 1.0 stable release.

## Install

Install Homebrew first, then run:

```bash
brew install --cask hungryZoo/tap/everydock
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/everyDock.app
open -a everyDock
```

## Update

Quit everyDock, then run:

```bash
brew update
brew upgrade --cask hungryZoo/tap/everydock
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/everyDock.app
open -a everyDock
```

Upgrade preserves settings. Uninstall/reinstall resets them. This release includes `everyDock-0.4.1-arm64.zip` and `SHA256SUMS`. Download both into one directory and verify with `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS`.
